notices.boundary_unsure: Start marker is the third occurrence of NOTICE OF CANCELLATION in the block (the first is inside the statement 'SEE THE ATTACHED NOTICE OF CANCELLATION FORM', the second the lead-in 'captioned "NOTICE OF CANCELLATION"'). The end is the form's last line; the statute then continues 'and the seller shall complete both copies ...', which is an instruction to the seller and is not cut. The researcher's extract flattened the form's address block, so the lines '(Name of Seller), AT Address of Seller / ____ (Place of Business) NOT LATER THAN MIDNIGHT OF / ____ ____ (Date)' print in that scrambled layout exactly as in the file.

changes.new: For a sale at the customer's home (Personal Property Law 426(6)), business day means every day except Sunday and nine named holidays, so Saturday counts.
changes.support: Business days under Article 10-A include Saturdays (426(6)).

unsure: NY-cancel and NY-insurance: GBL 771(1)(h) and (i) prescribe content but no sentence, so no text is loaded; the owner writes the wording.
Lien Law 71-a(3)(e) bold statement was not added: the file says it applies to new residential construction sales, not home improvement contracts.
GOL 5-903 (cleaning auto-renewal): the file says whether a recurring cleaning contract is a service contract on real property is a reading the text does not settle, so cleaning was left unchanged.
NY-lien: printed on contracts over $500 (GBL 771 applies to home improvement contracts over $500 per the existing applies); the cut is the quoted notice only, without the closing period.

NY-ppl428-statement and NY-ppl428-form: the builder only knows 'sold at the customer's home', but the statute covers any sale agreed away from the seller's place of business. The oral notice in 428(2) and the refund-policy disclosure in 428(4) are not part of the cut and are not printed. The form's address block is scrambled in the file's extract and is printed as extracted.
